entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-5588-rp99-5fjh: Moov signedxml: Unauthenticated denial of service in exclusive XML canonicalization
entry.content:
Moov signedxml: Unauthenticated denial of service in exclusive XML canonicalization

Aliases: CVE-2026-113729

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/moov-io/signedxml — fixed in 1.4.1

Exclusive XML canonicalization (`http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#`) in `github.com/moov-io/signedxml` copied the entire accumulated namespace map at every node during `ValidateReferences()`, before any reference digest or signature check. For a chain of nested elements that each declare many unused namespace prefixes, that produced **O(m × depth²)** time and peak memory (`m` = prefixes per level). `beevik/etree` caps tree depth (~1024), but `m` is unbounded, so a small attacker-controlled document (on the order of 1 MB) could drive multi-gigabyte allocations and OOM the process. No valid signature, matching certificate, or authentication is required. This is the library’s core path for SAML / WS-Federation service providers, which canonicalize attacker-supplied XML prior to authen…

## Summary The OpenChoreo API server authorized `PUT .../workflowruns/{runName}` against ownership metadata taken from the request body, while the object it actually mutated was selected by the URL path. Nothing forced the two to agree. A `WorkflowRun`'s membership in a project and component is carried entirely by its `openchoreo.dev/project` and `openchoreo.dev/component` labels. Because the `workflowrun:update` check read those labels from the submitted object rather than the stored one, a caller holding `workflowrun:update` on one component could name a run belonging to a different project or component in the URL, supply labels for the component they legitimately control, pass the check, and have the unrelated run rewritten with their own ownership labels. The namespace is taken from…

Coraza body processor has a JSON key collision that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass OWASP CRS inspection

Aliases: CVE-2026-114099, GO-2026-6692

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/corazawaf/coraza/v3 — fixed in 3.8.1

### Summary Coraza's JSON body processor converts nested JSON properties into dot-separated `ARGS_POST` names without escaping dots contained in literal property names. Two distinct JSON properties can therefore collapse into the same Coraza variable An unauthenticated attacker can place a malicious value in a nested property and then overwrite only Coraza's representation with a harmless dotted property: ```json { "account": { "role": "1' OR '1'='1" }, "account.role": "safe" } ``` Coraza stores both properties as `ARGS_POST:json.account.role`; the later value `safe` replaces the SQL-injection value. Standard backend JSON parsers preserve the two distinct properties and expose the malicious nested value as `account.role`. This bypasses the complete current OWASP Core Rule Se…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-3wr7-993q-jrff: Coraza: Multipart filename* (RFC 5987) charset restriction lets a decoy filename bypass FILES-based rules
entry.content:
Coraza: Multipart filename* (RFC 5987) charset restriction lets a decoy filename bypass FILES-based rules

Aliases: CVE-2026-114101, GO-2026-6691

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/corazawaf/coraza/v3 — fixed in 3.8.1

## Summary Coraza extracts a multipart file upload's filename using Go's standard-library `mime.ParseMediaType`, which only decodes the RFC 5987/6266 extended `filename*` `Content-Disposition` parameter when its declared charset is exactly `us-ascii` or `utf-8`. Any other charset — including `iso-8859-1`, which RFC 5987 explicitly permits — is silently dropped by the stdlib, with no error and no fallback signal. This lets an attacker present one filename to Coraza and a different one to the backend application in the same request. ## Affected variables `FILES` (documented as *"the original filenames as submitted by the client in the multipart upload"*), `FILES_SIZES`, and the file-vs-field routing decision that determines whether a part is tracked as a file at all. `MULTIPART_FILENAME`…

Argo CD repo-server command injection via crafted SSH repository SOCKS5 proxy URL

Aliases: BIT-argo-cd-2026-55797, CVE-2026-55797, GO-2026-6701

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2
  • github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 — fixed in 3.3.15
  • github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 — fixed in 3.4.10
  • github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 — fixed in 3.5.4
  • github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 — fixed in 3.6.0-rc2

### Impact Argo CD runs a shell command in the repo-server when it clones or fetches an SSH Git repository that has a proxy URL. The proxy host and port are copied into an SSH `ProxyCommand`. A host that contains shell metacharacters breaks out of that command and runs in the repo-server. All versions from v2.11.0 onward are affected, including every currently supported release. v2.10.20 and earlier are not. The behavior was introduced in [9b27aeb1a4](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/9b27aeb1a4fb15d11a0f01cad65dea1fdfc60205) (2024-01-09, [#15864](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/15864)), the change that added SOCKS5 proxy support for SSH Git URLs, and was first released in v2.11.0. The repository must use SSH. `http`, `https`, and `socks5` proxy URLs all take this path…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5: kin-openapi: Nil-pointer dereference panic in openapi3filter for OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas missing items
entry.content:
kin-openapi: Nil-pointer dereference panic in openapi3filter for OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas missing items

Aliases: CVE-2026-97394

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/getkin/kin-openapi — fixed in 0.143.0

### Summary A nil-pointer dereference in `openapi3filter` lets any unauthenticated client crash a request handler with a single HTTP request against an OpenAPI **3.1** operation that declares `type: array` **without** `items`. OpenAPI 3.1 (JSON Schema 2020-12) permits omitting `items`, and `doc.Validate()` accepts such schemas with `Schema.Items == nil`. Request/response decoders then dereference `Items` with no nil check. The panic is **deterministic (100%)** on every request to the affected operation. There is no `recover()` in `openapi3filter`; under handlers without per-request recover the process can exit. ### Details **Spec-validation asymmetry.** OpenAPI 3.0 rejects array schemas that omit `items` ([`openapi3/schema.go`](https://github.com/getkin/kin-openapi/blob/master/openapi3/…
